unit.title: Numbers Beyond 10 and Making Sense of Amounts

contentBlocks.text: Last week you compared groups of objects. Today, compare written numbers directly — without needing to count objects each time!

When comparing two written numbers, the bigger number represents more, and the smaller number represents less — this matches counting order: numbers later in the counting sequence (6, 7, 8...) are greater than numbers earlier in it (1, 2, 3...). For example, comparing 7 and 4: since 7 comes after 4 when counting, 7 is greater. Practice by comparing pairs of written numbers and saying which is greater, using the counting sequence to check yourself if you're unsure.
You can now compare written numbers directly, using what you know about counting order. Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Compare two written numerals (1-10) and identify which is greater
Use the counting sequence to justify which number is greater
materialsNeeded: A number line or counting chart (optional)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review comparing groups of objects from last week.
2. Introduce comparing written numbers using the counting-order idea, with the 7-vs-4 example.
3. Practice 2-3 more comparisons together, checking against a number line or counting chart if helpful.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Close by comparing two numbers the child picks themselves.
differentiationTips: Struggling: keep a number line or counting chart visible for every comparison, so the child can physically point to check their answer
Ready for more: ask the child to compare three numbers at once and put them in order from least to greatest
This connects directly to the counting sequence practiced since week 1 — worth naming that connection explicitly
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. 7 is greater than 4. 2. 3 is less than 8. 3. 9 is greater than 6. 4. 2 is less than 5.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core standards K.CC.6/K.CC.7: comparing numbers using written numerals, building on last week's group-comparison work with objects.

generationData.instructions: For each pair, write which number is greater.
